name: Em's DEV firmware (md-26912-190450)
about: Tag 'DEV '. DSP2, DSP1 and both data slots are byte-identical to stock 1.63. The ColdFire slot is 1.63 with about 300 small in-place patches (addresses preserved), re-packed. It boots like X.13 (boot routine at 0x2be00) but unpacks a smaller add-on to 0x2ee000, which unpacks 19 further pieces through a scatter table at flash 0xf0000. That table holds absolute flash offsets, so nothing after the DSP2 slot may move (the DSP2 slot keeps its length).
notes: Boot: 0x20003a jumps to 0x2be00: pea $2ee000; pea $e96e0; jsr $1c4 (boot-block NRV2B); addq #8; jsr $2ee000; jmp $213a0c. Same shape as X.13's, with operands at 0x2be08 and 0x2be1c.

Scatter: the add-on at 0x2ee0dc does lea $f0000,a0 and unpacks 19 (flash, RAM) pairs through $1c4, each an 8-byte header followed by NRV2B data. They fill RAM 0x2c0000..0x2e5470 without overlaps; the last stream ends at 0xfbde6, the end of the container. No other code in the add-on, the scatter routine or the changed ColdFire code holds an address in flash 0xe0000..0x100000, so 0xfbde8..0x100000 (16,920 bytes) is free for the patcher's RAM image, patch list and boot routine.

DSP2: the only runtime DSP write is at 0x2ee038, entered from the OS DSP boot at 0x201112 (jmp, returning to 0x201118), the same hook X.13 uses. Through the host-write routine $1000756 it writes 0x3cb words from RAM 0x2d8216 (scatter entry 8) to P:0x13b600..0x13b9ca, then init/trigger/render dispatch entries at 0x145af6/0x145bb7/0x145c78 + ID for the IDs in descriptors 0x2dbffa/0x2dbfa4/0x2dbf4e (GND-SN 1, GND-SW 4, GND-PU 5). No other code references $1000756, $100074c or the OS DSP interface 0x20a800..0x20ad00. The uploaded code branches only inside 0x13b600..0x13b9ca, has no p: accesses, touches only y:(r6+n) and x:(r4)+ with r4=0/m4=$1f, and reads x:$148000+. The patcher's DSP2 regions therefore start at 0x13b9cb.

RAM: DEV's pieces sit at 0x2c0000..0x2e5470 and 0x2ee000..0x2f55a4. None of its code holds an address in 0x2bc000..0x2c0000 (0x2b0bee and 0x2b034d are 1.63's own variables, below the heap start 0x2b7148). It never calls the heap (no call into the malloc module 0x245000..0x245b80 or sbrk 0x2139d6). Its heap ceiling at 0x2139f8 is 0x2c0000 (1.63: 0x300000); the patch list lowers it to 0x2bc000, as on X.13. The RAM window is 0x2bc000..0x2bd000 for the RAM image and 0x2be100..0x2bef60 for the dynamic-label segment.

Family table: DEV keeps 1.63's family count routines 0x22c1a0 (lea $252396 at 0x22c1a8) and 0x235350 (adda #$25239a at 0x235368), which X.13 moved into its add-on. Its machine-select page (scatter entry at 0x2c0000) reads names at 0x2c15b8/0x2c1622/0x2c168c/0x2c16f6 (lea $252396) and lists at 0x2c1c2e (lea $25239a). All of these are patched to point at the patcher's family table. It also reads the ROM family's list at 0x2523da directly; that stays valid because the patcher's table keeps the base's entries first. DEV's own GND/TRX lists (0x2f1800/0x2f181c) are copied into the new table unchanged. Nothing writes the family or descriptor table at run time; 0x2c0374, 0x2c152e, 0x2c69a6, 0x2c6cd8 and 0x2c6e36 read the descriptor table in place.

Lineage sites: every one holds 1.63's value except the heap ceiling (0x2c0000, see RAM). The patch-sites gate checks each one on every build. CTR-range tests: the lineage's 22 plus three of DEV's own, found by engine/src/scan.ts. The conditioning callbacks DEV adds to 20 TRX/EFM descriptors keep the 1.63 calling convention (out 4(sp), params 8(sp)).
DSP1: the DSP1 drive runs through the OS loop's SRAM sender call at 0x100056a. Its response laws have not yet been verified by listening.

hostSend.evidence: Plays with the reorder applied at all 10 sender references, in the emulator and on hardware. DEV runs MIDI through its own per-block queue (add-on 0x2f217a, entered from the DSP interrupt at 0x262788).

unmuteFix.why: DEV enters its own add-on code from the sequencer's tick handler and buffer toggle, so the sequencer the fix is written against is not there.

midiChroma.why: DEV feeds MIDI through its own per-block queue in its add-on (entered from the DSP interrupt), neither X.14's real-time path nor OS 1.63's MIDI task: not implemented.
